Which websites does AI rely on? What sources do ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity cite when they recommend a product, and how often does a brand's own website show up?
AI visibility, GEO (generative engine optimization) and AI SEO: a source analysis.

We analyzed 1,371 live-search answers from ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity and the 3,769 source links they cited (12–19 Nov 2026, US and Turkey, 35 measurement areas).

Chapters
00:00 Which websites does AI rely on?
00:30 How we measured it
01:04 The most-cited websites
01:37 How visible is the brand's own website?
02:14 Every category has its own referee
02:51 Even in Turkish, foreign sites lead
03:20 AIs don't read the same number of sources
03:46 Example: smart ring source network
04:19 Example: Seattle coffee shops
04:56 The AI that doesn't search the web (Gemini)
05:36 Three steps for your brand
06:11 How to measure this for your brand
06:45 Free check

Key findings
• Most-cited site: Tom's Guide (140 answers), then TechRadar (97) and RTINGS (64). No brand website in the top eight.
• Consumer products: roughly 6 of every 100 sources are the brand's own website; software tools: roughly 26%.
• Even for questions asked in Turkish, TechRadar was cited most; only 13% of sources were .tr sites.
• Claude cited 4.6 sources per answer on average; ChatGPT cited 2.
• In Seattle, all 6 answers citing Yelp mentioned Storyville; Starbucks appeared in only 6 of 48 answers.

Correction note: the video says the different brand picks of two AIs are "a big part" due to the difference in sources cited. That is our interpretation; the data shows the difference, it does not prove the cause. Gemini comparisons use small samples (11–14 answers).

These are AI answers. Small samples; not representative of the whole market. Brand-site share is approximate: domains containing the brand name.
Independent measurement. We have no sponsorship or partnership with any brand shown.
